articles.headline: Colts' Sauce Gardner vows not to repeat 'embarrassing' effort
articles.description: Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner said he gave his team an "embarrassing" effort in London and vowed there would not be a repeat performance.
articles.headlineJa: コルツのソース・ガードナー、「恥ずべき」プレーの繰り返しをしないと誓う
articles.descriptionJa: コルツのコーナーバック、ソース・ガードナーは、ロンドンでの自身のプレーはチームにとって「恥ずべき」ものだったと述べ、二度と繰り返さないと誓った。
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner, reflecting on his performance in Sunday's victory over the Commanders in London, said he gave his team an "embarrassing" effort and vowed there would not be a repeat performance.

Gardner, the two-time first-team All-Pro traded to the Colts last season for two first-round picks, was referring to his glaring lack of pursuit and effort on certain plays against the Commanders. Some of the plays went viral on social media, leaving Gardner mortified.

"There was multiple plays where my effort was not there," Gardner said. "That's not what I stand for. That's not the type of person I am. That's not the type of player I am. And that'll never happen again."

One play that drew scrutiny on social media was an 87-yard, third-quarter catch-and-run by Commanders receiver Antonio Williams. Gardner was not responsible for Williams on the play, but he let up his pursuit when safety Cam Bynum looked as if he might make the tackle. But Williams stayed on his feet and continued toward the end zone, with defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore giving chase in an all-out sprint. Gardner appeared to be jogging behind the play.

The score was ultimately overturned by a penalty, but Gardner cringed when he watched it later. "That's the embarrassing feeling right there," he said. "Seeing other guys on the D-line running past me, that's the part that's like, 'Yo, that's crazy.'

"When I'm loafing and then I'm seeing him slide past me, it's like, 'Bro, that's embarrassing.' Yeah, that's unacceptable."

Gardner said he saw the flag thrown for an illegal shift before the catch and assumed the penalty would go against Washington. But that wasn't a justification, he said.

"I saw the flag get thrown, but they could have picked the flag up and then there's nothing I could say," he said. "So, no matter what, I've got to make sure I'm running to the ball."

Gardner had one of his worst statistical performances in the game as he was in coverage on two big plays for the Commanders.

One, a 47-yard touchdown to Treylon Burks, was a bit of a busted play. Burks paused his sideline route and looked back for the ball, but it had not yet been thrown. He then continued down the field and quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis delivered it late, with Burks making the catch after Gardner lost track of him. On the other play, a 48-yard completion to Dyami Brown, Gardner was in perfect position but didn't make a play on the well-thrown ball.

But the main issue, he said, was not the completions. It was his effort -- or lack thereof.

"Effort is not even really a coachable trait," Gardner said. "It's something that the coach going to talk to you about, but you can't really coach effort. I still got a crazy feeling just thinking about it. That's why I'm just ready to get to practice and just work on those habits."

articles.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: Cam Jurgens to Ravens, Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys
articles.description: Will Cam Jurgens boost the Ravens' protection? Can Joey Porter Jr. clean up the Cowboys' defense? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
articles.headlineJa: NFLトレード期限の評価：カム・ジャーゲンズがレイブンズへ、ジョーイ・ポーターJr.がカウボーイズへ
articles.descriptionJa: カム・ジャーゲンズはレイブンズのパスプロテクションを強化できるか？ジョーイ・ポーターJr.はカウボーイズのディフェンスを立て直せるか？11月の期限を前に、NFLのトレードを評価する。
articles.body:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, which will pass on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET.

When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here are our evaluations for the first three deals of trading season: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants, Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys and Cam Jurgens to the Ravens. Check back right through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

Eagles trade C Jurgens to Ravens

Ravens get: C Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pick

Eagles get: 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Ravens grade: D+

Eagles grade: A

First, Tyler Linderbaum walked in free agency. Then the Ravens lost Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic to injury, suddenly leaving them without a center. Last week, Baltimore moved first-round rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane to center but evidently doesn't see that as a long-term option.

So Baltimore turned to the trade market and dealt for Jurgens. It's an interesting and unusual move, because Jurgens is no stopgap. He's only 27 years old and is already on a long-term deal after signing an extension with the Eagles in 2025.

Jurgens moved from center to left guard in Week 2 after the Eagles placed guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve. It has not gone well. Jurgens ranks in the bottom three in both pass block and run block win rate at guard. But the Ravens are trading for Jurgens to have him play center.

In 2024, Jurgens was a Pro Bowl center who recorded pass block and run block win rates in the 80th and 50th percentiles, respectively. He made the Pro Bowl again in 2025, but his numbers slipped to the 65th and 39th percentile, respectively. He should be a stabilizing force for the Ravens -- perhaps an average to above-average center -- at what has suddenly become a position of need. But the cost is exorbitant.

The Ravens are surrendering a second-round pick (plus a swap of fifth- and seventh-round picks) for the right to pay a non-premium position player market price after this season. Jurgens is due a fully guaranteed $16 million next year. He's due $17 million (non-guaranteed) in 2028 and 2029. Jurgens' $17 million average per year for the duration of his contract makes him the fourth-highest-paid center in the league, behind only Linderbaum, Creed Humphrey and Aaron Brewer, per OverTheCap.com. By comparison, Connor McGovern, who had better numbers than Jurgens last season, makes a little over $13 million per year.

articles.headline: Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo in doubt for Liverpool vs. Man City clash
articles.description: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has cast doubt on the chances of Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo being fit to face Manchester City this weekend.
articles.headlineJa: リヴァプール対マン・シティ戦、アレクサンダー・イサクとコディ・ガクポの出場が危ぶれる
articles.descriptionJa: リヴァプールのアンドニ・イラオラ監督は、今週末のマンチェスター・シティ戦に向けて、アレクサンダー・イサクとコディ・ガクポが万全の状態で出場できるかどうかに疑問を呈した。
articles.body:
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has cast doubt on the chances of Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo being fit to face Manchester City this weekend.

The pair both returned home early from international duty with Sweden and the Netherlands due to thigh and ankle problems, respectively.

- Liverpool can't afford to be without Isak, Gakpo for daunting October fixture list

- Mock draft: How would Premier League teams pick if Man City cheating scandal took a turn?

- How top Premier League clubs view Man City's guilty verdict

Having inherited Hugo Ekitike's long-term Achilles injury, Iraola could be without his two senior forwards for Sunday's highly-anticipated clash, City's first match since an independent commission found them guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

"I think Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo both have had to leave the national teams with injuries," Iraola told beIN SPORTS.

"Now it's a matter of if they are going to recover in time to help us in the next game or not. But right now they are both injured."

Iraola did not mention the status of center back Jérémy Jacquet, who was omitted from France's 4-1 victory over Belgium on Monday with a hamstring strain.

The visit of City is the biggest game of Iraola's Liverpool career so far and despite four wins and three draws his side have struggled to find anything close to their best form.

"We've been unbeaten but they've won all of them, so it makes a big difference in their side," he said. "I think we need to be very, very good if we want to beat City because they've been especially offensively scoring a lot of goals lately.

"We know the names that are very dangerous. But I think also we've shown good defensive improvements lately and I hope we can defend the threats that they have and also hurt them on the other side."

The international break will have done little to help the consistency Iraola needs as he tries to get a squad which hugely underperformed last season to successfully adopt his methods.

"I think the goal is quite clear and I think everyone understands what we are trying to build," he said. "Try to be more intense, more vertical, but also you want to control the games.

"For example, I think in Newcastle [a 2-2 draw] we played a good game but probably we conceded two goals in transition [and] you want to control a little bit more of the games.

"I think lately we've been controlling the games much more but we lacked a little bit [of] this offensive fluidity that we had in the first game. So, now it's a matter of balancing this a little.

"Obviously we want to attack very well and defend very well but sometimes you have to choose or you have to adapt the team to what you prefer or what is the requirements of a specific game and we are trying to balance all this."

articles.headline: Another bad Man United run has Carrick feeling the heat. Should he be?
articles.description: Michael Carrick is hardly unique in that he brought hope to Man United, but is he on course to become the latest coach to be fired midseason?
articles.headlineJa: マン・Uの再びの不調でキャリックにプレッシャー。解任されるべきか？
articles.descriptionJa: マイケル・キャリックがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドに希望をもたらしたことは決して珍しいことではないが、彼はシーズン途中で解任される最新の監督となってしまうのだろうか？
articles.body:
For many supporters, the Manchester United cycle appears to be back in full swing. An uptick in form under Michael Carrick renewed hope that the club could finally be moving in the right direction toward the end of the 2025-26 campaign, but it has been followed by a difficult start to the new season and pressure is mounting on the head coach.

It was a similar story for José Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim. Moments of optimism -- some briefer than others -- and then a sharp downturn that led to a seemingly inevitable parting of ways.

United have sacked managers midway through each of their past two seasons -- Ten Hag in October 2024 and Amorim in January 2026. Take it back further and managers have been dismissed midseason in four of the past eight completed campaigns. The scrutiny on Carrick -- who signed only a two-year contract as long-term head coach in May -- has increased with United winning just two of their first seven games in all competitions.

A last-minute equalizer to secure a 1-1 draw at Fulham before the international break prevented a run of three defeats in a row but Carrick -- and the club in general -- is under the spotlight again.

The international break has been dominated by Manchester City and their legal case with the Premier League. United could end up with millions in compensation, but the most immediate -- and welcome -- consequence of the verdict breaking is that the spotlight has been focused on the Etihad and not Old Trafford.

Will that remain the case after Saturday's visit of Tottenham Hotspur, another club in turmoil? Or do we have reason to doubt Carrick's position as manager?

Is history repeating?

There's certainly a familiar feel about it all. Ten Hag was sacked after United won four of their 13 games in all competitions to open the 2024-25 season. Amorim survived a start of two wins from seven but was gone by January.

Solskjaer lasted 17 games in 2021-22 despite finishing second the season before. Mourinho also finished second in 2017-18 but was dismissed just 24 games into the 2018-19 campaign. It's evidence of how quickly things can unravel at Old Trafford.

Carrick won 12 of 17 games last season after being appointed caretaker boss in January, suffering just two defeats and recording impressive wins over Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool along the way. No Premier League manager won more points during the same period as United finished third to qualify for the UEFA Champions League.

But just like the achievements of Mourinho and Solskjaer, it has been quickly forgotten. The defeat to newly promoted Hull City on the opening weekend put Carrick on the back foot immediately. The performance against 10-man Manchester City was poor, and losing to Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup after leading 2-0 after 10 minutes was damaging.

articles.headline: Tottenham's Mathys Tel equals France under-21 goalscoring record
articles.description: Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.
articles.headlineJa: トッテナムのマティス・テル、フランスU-21の得点記録に並ぶ
articles.descriptionJa: マティス・テルは、代表ウィーク中のフランスU-21での得点感覚を、プレミアリーグのシーズン立て直しに向けたトッテナムの戦いに持ち込みたいと考えている。
articles.body:
Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.

Tel has yet to score for Spurs this season but hit a hat-trick in a 7-1 win over Switzerland in Orleans on Tuesday night as France, who had already qualified for the 2027 European U21 Championship, completed their group campaign unbeaten with eight victories.

With 17 goals, Tel, who also scored in two other games over the break, has equalled Odsonne Edouard's record for France U21s and could have put himself into contention for a senior call-up to Zinedine Zidane's squad for the Nations League games in November.

"My brother had been nagging me about it [the goals record] for months. In the end it was in the back of my mind," Tel told reporters, as quoted in L'Equipe.

"With qualification [achieved], there was a different kind of motivation that allowed me to give my best, so now I am very happy."

Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham slumped to the bottom of the table ahead of the international break, with a 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa a third loss from their five opening Premier League games.

The boss welcomed former player and first-team coach Gus Poyet to the training ground on Tuesday and appeared in good spirits as the pair chatted on the sidelines in a video on the club's social media account.

Spurs travel to Manchester United on Saturday and have a few fitness concerns following the international break.

Right-back Pedro Porro has been carrying a hamstring injury which saw him pull out the Spain squad ahead of the extended three-week window.

Defender Jan Paul van Hecke was then sent home early from the Netherlands camp with a foot problem, which could keep him out of contention at Old Trafford.

Fellow Dutchman Micky van de Ven picked up a minor hand injury after being accidentally stepped on during the win over Serbia in Eindhoven and was forced off late on, but the Spurs captain is expected to be involved.

Speaking after the match, Netherlands manager Xavi told reporters: "He is okay. He felt dizzy because he suffered with his finger. It is not a big injury."

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta signs new four-year Arsenal contract
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract to extend his stay at Arsenal, the Premier League champions confirmed.
articles.headlineJa: ミケル・アルテタ、アーセナルと4年間の新契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグ覇者のアーセナルは、ミケル・アルテタが残留を決める新契約に署名したことを発表した。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract to extend his stay at Arsenal until 2030, the Premier League champions confirmed. 

ESPN previously reported that Arteta was set to pen a new contract. His previous deal was due to expire at the end of this season. 

The Spaniard led Arsenal to their first Premier League title in 23 years last season and also won the FA Cup in 2020. 

"It's a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal," he said in a statement.

"This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue.

"We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together."

He joined the club in December 2019 after serving as assistant manager at Manchester City, and is currently the longest-serving head coach in the Premier League. 

Co-chairs Stan and Josh Kroenke said: "It has been an incredible journey so far and we are excited for what lies ahead in this special relationship. Last season was an incredible moment in Arsenal's history, a moment in which we created memories that will last a lifetime. We're determined to create many more in the years ahead.

"We share a special bond with Mikel. We are so proud of everything we have achieved since he returned to the club in 2019."

Arsenal have also confirmed that Arteta's coaching staff have also renewed their deals for four more years.

articles.headline: Basketball Power Index: NBA projections, playoff chances for 2026-27 season
articles.description: ESPN's Basketball Power Index projections for the 2026-27 NBA season are out, including a ranking of all 30 teams.
articles.headlineJa: バスケットボール・パワー・インデックス：2026-27年NBAシーズンの展望とプレーオフ進出の可能性
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNによる2026-27年NBAシーズンのバスケットボール・パワー・インデックスの予測が発表され、全30チームのランキングが公開された。
articles.body:
The NBA season starts Tuesday, Oct. 20, and ESPN has multiple previews to guide readers, including a ranking of the top 100 players, a look at the top players in new places and capsules on each team, with the most important stats that affect teams' win-loss records.

Now it's time for a season preview using ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI), which evaluates two different strength measures for all 30 NBA teams: one based on players currently available, and the other based on players who should be available during the playoffs. Then, to create preseason projections, the BPI takes into account win totals from the betting market in conjunction with each team's schedule and other factors, simulating the season thousands of times, with the results forming these projections.

Once the season begins, the BPI watches what happens in games and updates both its current BPI and its playoff BPI. There are numerous benefits to this, particularly that it adjusts game predictions on the fly when there are reports of players missing games. If Giannis Antetokounmpo is going to miss a game, for instance, the BPI marks down the Miami Heat's chance to win that game by an amount suggested by history. Sometimes, those injury reports are late or inaccurate (ahem, Joel Embiid) and it annoys us, the BPI and the league as a whole. But don't hold that against the BPI's model.

One thing the BPI isn't seeing this season is a secret prediction edge over Las Vegas. There aren't major deviations in this model's rankings from what Vegas is forecasting.

Let's dig into the projections, including how it ranks teams from 1 to 30 and which teams have the best chance to win the NBA Finals.

Jump to a section:

1-30 team rankings

NBA playoff projections

NBA Finals projections

More takeaways

Regular-season projections

The BPI values shown are the current numbers, not the version for the playoffs. The Golden State Warriors are down at No. 20, reflecting the absence of Jimmy Butler III, who tore his ACL in January and could return around midseason. The Warriors would be No. 12 if they were at full strength.

There is only one other team with an injury causing significant deviations between their current and playoff power: Embiid and the Philadelphia 76ers. That's because we know from history Embiid is going to miss games -- he has played 41 games per season since he was drafted and has played just 96 over the past three seasons -- and he is a good enough player that it matters. With Embiid, the Sixers have the third-best playoff BPI, consistent with the expectation they are among the favorites to come out of the East.

There are a few things to note from the overall league rankings. First, the Denver Nuggets finished last season as the league's best offense in the league, and the BPI isn't going to argue that they got worse. They've been in the top six on offense for seven years now. They're, of course, led by Nikola Jokic, who was the No. 1-ranked player in our top 100.

articles.headline: We don't get Man City guilty verdict without hacker Rui Pinto, but it doesn't make him a hero
articles.description: The Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its core, wouldn't have been possible without Football Leaks and its founder, Rui Pinto. However, he is a complicated figure, with light and dark to his actions.
articles.headlineJa: ハッカーのルイ・ピントがいなければマン・シティの有罪判決はなかったが、彼がヒーローなわけではない
articles.descriptionJa: イングランドのサッカー界を根底から揺るがしているマンチェスター・シティの事案は、「フットボール・リークス」とその創設者ルイ・ピントがいなければ不可能だっただろう。しかし、彼の行動には光と影があり、複雑な人物である。
articles.body:
It's worth reminding ourselves that the Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its foundation, would never have seen the light of day without a spiky-haired college dropout turned self-taught hacker named Rui Pinto.

Had he not obtained and shared more than 70 million documents with the German magazine Der Spiegel starting in 2016, culminating in the publication of their massive "Football Leaks" investigation two years later, there would have been no investigation of City -- not by UEFA, not by the Premier League, not by any of the other bodies that may get involved once the current process is concluded.

Simply put, there would have been no legal basis for anyone to do this. We would have had an alternate reading of history -- one where City get new owners, Abu Dhabi United Group in 2009, spend a ton of money, watch their revenues skyrocket and dominate the game, all the while complying with every single financial regulation set before them. (The only exception was in 2014, when they breached UEFA's Financial Fair Play regulations and eventually signed a three-year settlement agreement.)

Whatever the ultimate outcome of the City case -- whether it results in expulsion from the Premier League and Sheikh Mansour having to shell out hundreds of millions in fines and compensation, or somehow ends in the club getting most, if not all, of the charges overturned on appeal -- this should be a massive wake-up call to those running the game. The message: football needs better oversight and more transparency.

Whichever way the dust settles, this much is obvious: the system failed. Either City did participate in a massive "sham" (to quote from the verdict), effectively cheating while the system failed to notice and act, or the Premier League is so inept that it has somehow been duped by a conspiracy of legacy clubs into conducting an ultimately futile eight-year investigation. Neither outcome is good; in fact, both are embarrassingly bad for the world's most successful league.

What would better oversight and transparency look like? How about something like we have in the NFL, where information about salaries, sponsorships and other revenue is shared not just with the league, but with teams around the league itself as well as the players' union. That creates a virtuous cycle of self-policing and makes it much harder to engage in financial skullduggery. (Harder, but not impossible, as old-school San Francisco 49ers fans will confirm.)

In the Premier League, far too much is a closely guarded secret in the name of "competitive advantage" -- clubs, not just City, disclose as little as legally allowed as if they were running some normal business, not a hugely important public trust like the world's most popular sport.

All of which brings us back to Pinto.

articles.headline: Man City glory can't be taken from players - Kyle Walker
articles.description: Manchester City's glory years cannot be taken away from the players, according to former captain Kyle Walker.
articles.headlineJa: マン・シティの栄光は選手たちのものだ ― カイル・ウォーカー
articles.descriptionJa: 元キャプテンのカイル・ウォーカーによれば、マンチェスター・シティの黄金時代が築いた栄光を奪い去ることはできないという。
articles.body:
Manchester City's glory years cannot be taken away from the players, according to former captain Kyle Walker.

City have appealed against last week's seismic judgment of an independent commission that they broke Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

Walker spent eight years at City from 2017 to 2025, winning the Champions League as well as 12 major domestic honours.

Speaking on talkSPORT, Burnley right-back Walker said: "Obviously it doesn't look great. I know it's in an appeal stage so, for me to start commenting on the legal action and everything like that, probably it's not going to do myself justice or anyone involved in it.

"But, at a personal level, I can say the lads, we spent many and many a great year celebrating many trophies and everything like that and that's something that, whatever happens, they can't take away from us because we've experienced them nights.

"So, whatever will be, will be, and it's just down to the appeal now and what goes from there."

The independent commission concluded more than £830 million ($1.08 bn) of owner funding was used to inflate revenues and enable the club to comply with Premier League and UEFA financial rules through a series of "sham" arrangements over a nine-year period.

A City statement released last Friday read: "The club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case."

- We don't get Man City guilty verdict without hacker Rui Pinto, but it doesn't make him a hero

- Transfer rumors, news: PSG eye Man City midfielder Cherki amid Premier League charges

- Man City punishment must be 'three to five years' - Jamie Carragher

Walker admitted it is not an easy subject for former City players to discuss, adding: "It's something that we probably don't want to talk about because we want to be looked upon as winning them trophies, winning them the right way.

"It's very difficult because we've worked very hard for them, and not just us, I look at the fans as well.

"I look at the fans that have travelled up and down the country, travelled abroad to Istanbul when we won the treble and stuff like that, and they deserve that night as well."
